findings.title: New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: order() is added as an abstract interface method with no default implementation. Any CryptoProvider implementation outside this repository (custom server providers, downstream Elytron/FIPS variants, test doubles) will fail to compile and, if compiled against the old interface, throw AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration sorts providers by order(). This should be a default method (e.g. returning a defined default priority) so existing providers keep working and only providers needing precedence override it.

findings.title: Equal-order providers are now silently chosen non-deterministically instead of failing fast
findings.body: Previously detectProvider() threw IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. Now it sorts by order() descending and silently ignores the rest, but DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200. If two of those are co-present (e.g. default + Elytron in WildFly, or default + FIPS), the winner depends only on unspecified ServiceLoader iteration order among equal keys, so a non-FIPS provider could be selected in FIPS mode or vice versa with only a debug log. Equal top orders should either retain the fail-fast error or have a deterministic, documented tie-break.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore provider, not BouncyCastle
findings.body: The method contract in CryptoProvider is to return the BouncyCastle (or BCFIPS) security provider, and callers use it for BC-specific algorithms and provider names. This implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which on a stock JDK is typically the SUN provider, not BouncyCastle. Any authz-client code path (or synced keycloak-client code path) that consults getBouncyCastleProvider() expecting BC capabilities will get the wrong provider and can fail with NoSuchAlgorithm/NoSuchProvider or behave differently. It should return null like WildFlyElytronProvider if no BC provider is available, or an actually-registered BC provider.

findings.title: ES384/ES512 tests use a P-256 key and only assert round-trip equality
findings.body: The shared constructor creates one KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() key, which defaults to a 256-bit curve, and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512. asn1derToConcatenatedRS merely zero-pads/truncates r and s to algorithm.getSignatureLength()/2, so the round-trip assertion passes for ES384/ES512 even though no P-384/P-521 key or real signature of that size is ever produced or verified. The test never verifies the produced DER signature with Signature.verify(), so conversion defects for larger curves or leading-zero r/s values would go undetected. Each algorithm should generate a key on its matching curve and verify the converted signature cryptographically.
